10: The ear of the spirit will bring the first tidings, not so somebody can pen a master’s dissertation but so that people can lead lives that forge evolution. The Teaching can say to the sensitive: On awakening, recall the distant worlds; on going to sleep, recall the distant worlds. (NEC, 29)
11:
It is one thing to discuss the distant worlds in abstract terms, and quite another to realize that you yourself are participating in them. Only a seeker who has not barred his own way to the path of beauty can understand how near he is to the manifestation of the distant worlds.

The ear can catch fragments of the Great Breath, but it is knowledge of the spirit that gives man a place in Infinity. (NEC, 30)
12: I am telling you to keep the Teaching simple. Complicated expressions are unnecessary, because life is beautiful in its simplicity. Just as one often has to dig around a plant, one inevitably has to make repetitions. (NEC, 31)
13:
What sort of mobility can [the spirit] exercise on the face of the Earth? In the earthly sphere, what thoughts is it able to share?

People ask why We waste so much energy on the Earth. It is not for the sake of the Earth but for the purpose of repairing the path. When someone rips up the rails with malicious intent, often the engineer takes a great deal of time to repair them. Were We immediately able to transfer from the Earth those possessing awareness of the Cosmos, would there be anything preventing Us from acting on Our desire to do so? In fact, We are striving to accelerate this process. I feel it is quite possible that cosmic conditions may soon allow commencement of such activities involving interaction with the distant worlds. This process calls for all the thoughts about beauty and all the impetuosity that you can muster. And remember, above beauty, so called, is an all-encompassing concept—the betterment of the Cosmos. The rainbow ray may surpass the imagination. Silver is what gives birth to the rainbow. Viewed under earthly conditions, the rainbow resembles makeup seen up close. Few can sense beforehand the beauty of the supermundane rainbow. (NEC, 35)
14: The gardener knows when it is time to gather the flowers, for he is the one who planted the seeds now unseen. (NEC, 42)
15:
The essence of striving to the distant worlds lies in assimilating awareness of our life on them. The idea that there may possibly be life on them is, as it were, a canal for our consciousness to approach them. Indeed, one has to break open the current of this consciousness as if one were digging a canal. People are able to swim, but a significant number of them do not do so. The evidence that exists concerning the distant worlds does not attract humanity at all. It is time to sow the seed of this idea in the human brain.

Those without family or fortune can most easily accept this thought. Earthly ties are not as lasting for them. The well-off have the most trouble accepting. (NEC, 44)
16:
You already know the usefulness of obstacles and the advantages of hardships. It could be that even terrors have their uses. Of course, for Us and for you there are no terrors in the ordinary sense. On the contrary, terror without fear turns into an act of cosmic beauty.

Could one possibly think about beauty without a chord of rapture? (NEC, 58)
17: Much can be forgiven someone who even in darkness has preserved the concept of the Teacher. The Teacher uplifts the dignity of the spirit. For Us the concept of the Teacher is like a lamp in the darkness. Thus, the Teacher can be called a beacon of responsibility. The ties with the Teaching are like a lifeline in the mountains. The Teacher appears the moment the spirit kindles. From that moment onward the Teacher is inseparable from the disciple. (NEC, 60)
18: Truly, one can look forward to all of the prophecies being fulfilled. I do not see any of the timeframes changing. Think over the envelope of events and understand how unimportant the exterior is: Only the inner meaning provides answers. That which has been sown for generations is beginning to stir; the seed is beginning to sprout. (NEC, 75)
19:
On the day when a new step is beginning, let us speak without reproach about this great era, a time when we are learning to break away from the Earth and, while in the body, are already communing with the Highest Worlds. . . .

My Word ought to establish you in the beauty of podvig. As we embark on the path, let us leave behind instructions for action and again focus our consciousness beyond the earthly. It is wonderful to be in possession of a subtle body when one’s spirit no longer feels disturbed before distant flights. Therefore, let us rejoice in each of the movements on the Earth’s crust . . .

To fly—what a beautiful word! In it there already lies a pledge that we will attain our destination. When things get difficult, think about flights; let each aspirant think about wings. To the bold ones I am sending all the currents of space! (NEC, 82)
20: Only a tested consciousness understands the value of a kernel of reality. Rulership is in neither crowns nor crowds, but rather in the cosmic expanse of ideas. Thus, the Teachings of Life complement each other, without any need to attract the multitudes. (NEC, 84)
21: Keep the air in your homes clean, send out your best wishes to those who are coming, and wait for Us eagerly. Let each community wait for its Teacher, for the community and the Teacher constitute the two ends of one column. Even when doing daily chores you need to remember the foundation of the house. Again we arrive at the need to alter the quality of the consciousness, for that makes the transition easy. (NEC, 91)
22:
Remember the treasure of the consciousness. The tremor of the substance of the Cosmos manifests the pulsation of the awakened consciousness. Indeed, the rainbow of knowledge issues from the tremor of consciousness. A visible stream from an invisible source.

Drawing on all the experiences of the past and all the attainments of the future, remember about consciousness. (NEC, 97)
23: Every school must be a true citadel of education. Schools should have a useful museum in which the students themselves take part. There should be a cooperative, and the students must be trained in such cooperation. All aspects of art must be included. Without the paths of beauty there can be no education. (NEC, 104)
24: While teaching students to respect useful inventions, the school will protect them from slavery to devices. As signs of darkness, all forms of slavery will be destroyed. The teacher will be an instructor and friend who leads the way by indicating the shortest, best path forward—not with a show of force but with a summoning smile. (NEC, 108)
25: Let the fundamentals of astronomy be included among the subjects of study, positioning it as an entryway to the distant worlds. By doing this schools will arouse the first thoughts about life in those worlds. Space will come alive, as studies on astrochemistry and rays enrich the students’ vision of the magnitude of the Universe. Young hearts will feel themselves to be not ants crawling on the earth’s crust but bearers of the spirit who are responsible for the planet. Let us focus attention on schools, because it is from them that cooperation will be established. Nothing will be created without cooperation. There will be no stability in governments or alliances so long as the same old selfishness holds sway. (NEC, 110)
26: Protect children from everything false: protect them from bad music, protect them from foul language, protect them from spurious competitions, and protect them from assertion of egoism, especially as you need to inculcate a love of continual learning. The muscles must not get the better of the mind and heart. What kind of heart takes a liking to blows of the fist? (NEC, 116)
27: Plants reach out to the light—this law of primordial consciousness is immutable. Follow the path of immutability and build life! Nothing is abstract, and life absorbs every thought. Therefore, be realists of the true reality. (NEC, 122)
28: Day and night Our coworkers are ready for all the radiance of the Cosmos. In readiness they will pass by day unseen, and at night they will find the resplendent path. Nothing disturbs you when you are constantly being disturbed. The seeker’s character prevents the ship from getting icebound. (NEC, 152)
29:
One can well imagine that the path of those bearing a mission is not a restful one. . . . But by human hands and feet is the World Community built, and in this lies the beauty of its construction.

It is rare, however, for the messenger of the Community to meet with a welcome in cities. The very soul of the city snarls at him. In fact, the very existence of the Community is denied in the city. The very atmosphere does not allow any rest to the messenger. . . .

Of course, awareness of cooperation-community is progressing, but the thinking of the narrow-minded is stuck in stagnation.

We summon coworkers who know the difficulties. We summon those who will not turn back. We summon those who know that joy is a special wisdom!

We may provide the most challenging information, but our advice leads to jubilation! (NEC, 156)
30:
The time has come when we shall say to each worker, “You belong to us!” When we shall revise the paths and the signs, starting from the celestial ones. When we shall abbreviate languages and expressions of thought. When we shall read the ancient verses for the last time.

. . . Without succumbing to superstition, we must survey the milestones of humanity’s development under the sign of the community. We must see how the victory of the community grew, kindling the fires of knowledge and beauty. True knowledge and beauty comprise the best community.

Let us select and affirm everything that is best, and the one who discerns what is best will become a community member. (NEC, 228)
31:
What are the signs of the Era of Shambhala? It is an age of truth and cooperation.

Study how the word “Shambhala” is uttered in the East. Try to delve into the thought underlying this concept, even in a small way. Try to understand the rhythm in how the narrative about Shambhala is structured, and you will sense a great reality that makes the chords of humanity vibrate. Let reason help you to ponder the values accumulated by the finest efforts and aspirations. The concept of Shambhala cannot be left out of the book Community.

Friends, understand what a tense and wondrous time this is! (NEC, 242)
01: The seed of labor dries up without the moisture of reciprocity. Let us not glance backward too often. Hurrying onward together, we will grow exhausted if we keep jostling each other. We will grasp something of wondrous significance if we give voice to the great concept—friend. It is possible to have a community made up of friends. (NEC, 4)
02: Cooperation must be based on robust rules. This accustoms the coworkers to order; that is, it helps them get into a rhythm. In this way the great laws of the Universe find expression even in everyday work. It is especially necessary to get used to constant work from childhood. Let the best evolution be built upon labor, adopting it as a measure of value. (NEC, 8)
03:
Through love of a favorite craft, an elevated quality will begin to pervade pure work. A beautiful quality will establish itself in the entirety of life. Nothing will remain in darkness. Ignorance will come to be considered a shameful crime. Darkness may be infectious, but Light is attractive. Therefore, let us proclaim love of a favorite craft, which uplifts all of life.

Science, point to the best quality. Science, attract the most powerful energies. Let the knowledge of the spirit shine above every workbench. (NEC, 10)
04: Respect for craftsmanship should be fostered, so that people see it as a mark of distinction. Ancient working communities, guilds, and workshops left evidence of their vitality. One can see how people honed their skills with perfection in mind. They knew how to look after each other and maintain the dignity of their community. So long as people do not learn to defend the dignity of their coworkers, they will not understand the happiness of contributing to the Common Good. (NEC, 12)
05: You can only reach Us in harmony. We have no need of being worshipped; rather, what We need is a certain quality of spirit, something like a harmonious lamp, one whose voltage matches Ours. A flickering lamp is unbearable for doing prolonged work. In everything the same laws apply, and under the law of justice the flickering lamp winds up hurting itself. I advise My lamps not to flicker. The generator is not damaged by the quality of the lamps, but when the voltage of a lamp does not match up, it often ends with a pitiable “pop!” Then the basic metal must be supplied once more. The same laws apply in everything. (NEC, 22)
06: There is no soulless justice, only radiant goalfitness. Precisely, glorious goalfitness can never tyrannize, but instead opens the beautiful gates. And the call of goalfitness fills space with a feeling of victory. The events and creations that follow the principle of goalfitness are not obsolete fragments but precious parts of the Cosmos. (NEC, 23)
07: Pure thought imbued with beauty points the way to truth. Teachings that require renunciation and obedience to prohibitions are given in condescension to people of limited consciousness. But in the case of someone with an expanded consciousness, there are no stop signs but rather steady progress without prohibitions. Beautified lives allow people to depart in freedom and abundance, in order to return as victors. A seeker who proceeds with awareness of beauty cannot be confused. Only confusion can obstruct the path. (NEC, 27)
08:
It is not quite right to say, “Beauty will save the world”; it is more precise to say, “Awareness of beauty will save the world.”

You can pass through the obstacles of ugliness on the way to the lighthouse of beauty, scattering seeds without number. When one is able to create a garden of beauty, there is nothing to fear. When the garden of the spirit admits the newcomers, there is no fatigue. (NEC, 27)
09: The Teaching of the New World will protect people from all kinds of distress. Indeed, only the shield of the Community can make sense of the sojourn on Earth. How incredibly beautiful it is to think about cooperation with the distant worlds! This cooperation, begun consciously, will draw new worlds into its orbit of interaction. And this heavenly cooperative will expand its possibilities without end. (NEC, 29)
